stances.claim: Two crucial documents have surfaced since last Sunday's column: the petitioners' Bacud 'Certification' that no record of payment exists in Branch 105 (which they argue proves BB is still perpetually disqualified), and BB's supporters' Land Bank 'Official Receipt' dated Dec. 27, 2001 showing P67,137.27 in LEASE RENTAL, INSTALLMENT, INTEREST, PRINCIPAL (which they argue triggers the five-year prescription under Section 12 of the OEC).
stances.rhetorical_move: two-document-frame as evidentiary inventory (presenting each side's best documentary evidence as the case's center of gravity)

stances.claim: The Bacud Certification is the wrong certifier -- Rowena Bacud is 'merely the OIC of Branch 105,' but final CA decisions are enforced through the courts of origin, and the official authorized to certify the receipt of fines (which become part of the Judiciary Development Fund) is the clerk of court of the entire RTC-QC station (Gregorio C. Tallud), which encompasses all 57 branches. If petitioners can secure a similar certification from Tallud, 'their argument could gain cogency.'
stances.rhetorical_move: wrong-official-as-evidentiary-defect (offering both critique AND remedy for the petitioner)

stances.claim: The Land Bank Official Receipt is facially vague -- it makes no reference to the CA disposition, which has TWO parts (deficiency income taxes to the BIR with legal-rate interest, and fines for the ITR-non-filing charges) -- and BB's supporters must explain how P67,137.27 is to be applied between the two items, why the receipt is adequate, and why the fines were paid to Land Bank rather than to the RTC-QC station clerk of court.
stances.rhetorical_move: two-part-disposition-then-receipt-mapping (forcing BB's side to demonstrate item-by-item correspondence)

stances.claim: Justice Jose Midas P. Marquez's promotion -- after a record 13 JBC nominations -- brings to six the number of SC justices from Ateneo de Manila (plus a seventh from Ateneo de Davao), easily besting the UP College of Law's traditional 'top producer' status with only three, with San Beda's three and UST/UE's one each rounding out the count.
stances.rhetorical_move: law-school-tally framing (institutional-affiliation accounting as significant biographical context)

stances.claim: Marquez is a 'homegrown SC justice' -- beginning his judicial career in 1991 as apprentice and later executive assistant before his 1993 law-school graduation, then law clerk of Senior Justice Josue N. Bellosillo (where CJ met him in 1995), then SC court administrator from January 2010 until promotion -- and as second-youngest member of the Court he will serve until his 70th birthday on February 16, 2036.
stances.rhetorical_move: biographical-arc tribute (presenting Marquez's institutional rise as exemplary)

notable_anecdotes: CJ flagging that the Land Bank receipt's column 'LEASE RENTAL, INSTALLMENT, INTEREST and PRINCIPAL' is in all caps in the original -- 'All caps in original' as parenthetical fidelity-marker -- underscoring that BB's exhibit does not even purport on its face to be a tax-and-fine payment, but a lease-rental receipt.

The 57-branch RTC-QC station detail -- a procedural fact that grounds CJ's argument that Bacud (Branch 105 OIC) is the wrong certifier -- making the column's central evidentiary critique turn on an internal court-administration technicality.

Justice Marquez's record-setting 13 JBC nominations before finally being promoted to the SC -- the most concentrated single biographical figure for institutional persistence in CJ's tributes to recent SC appointees.
CJ's first meeting with Marquez in 1995 in Senior Justice Josue N. Bellosillo's chambers -- making the column a quiet personal-lineage gesture alongside its forensic COC analysis.

The Ateneo-vs-UP law school tally -- six Ateneo de Manila + one Ateneo de Davao versus three UP, three San Beda, one UST, one UE -- the most explicit law-school census in CJ's column-corpus tributes to new SC justices.

The note that Marquez will serve until February 16, 2036, just months ahead of Justice Hernando (August 27, 2036) -- pinpointing a generational cohort that will sit on the Court for nearly 15 more years.

one_paragraph_summary: Picking up from last Sunday's column, Panganiban examines two crucial documents that have surfaced in the Bongbong Marcos COC cancellation case. The petitioners produced a 'Certification' from Rowena Sto. Tomas-Bacud, OIC of Branch 105 of the RTC-QC, stating there is no record on file of compliance with the October 31, 1997 Court of Appeals decision -- purporting to prove BB is still perpetually disqualified. BB's supporters produced a Land Bank 'Official Receipt' dated December 27, 2001 in the name of 'MARCOS JR. FERDINAND' showing P67,137.27 in LEASE RENTAL, INSTALLMENT, INTEREST, and PRINCIPAL -- purporting to trigger the five-year prescriptive period under Section 12 of the Omnibus Election Code. Panganiban's humble opinion: the Bacud Certification is from the wrong officer, because final CA decisions are enforced by the courts of origin and the proper certifier for fines (which become part of the Judiciary Development Fund) is Gregorio C. Tallud, clerk of court of the entire RTC-QC station made up of 57 branches; the petitioners' argument 'could gain cogency' if they secured a similar certification from him. The Land Bank Official Receipt, on the other hand, is facially vague: it makes no reference to the CA disposition, which has two parts -- (a) deficiency income taxes payable to the BIR with legal-rate interest, and (b) fines of P2,000 per charge for 1982-1984 ITRs and P30,000 for 1985 ITR with surcharges -- and BB's supporters must explain how P67,137.27 is to be applied between them, and why the fines were paid to Land Bank rather than to the RTC-QC station clerk of court. He closes by felicitating Justice Jose Midas P. Marquez on his recent SC promotion after a record 13 JBC nominations, noting that this brings to six the number of SC justices from Ateneo de Manila (plus a seventh from Ateneo de Davao), easily besting UP's traditional 'top producer' status with three (San Beda also three; UST and UE one each). Marquez -- 'homegrown' to the Court since 1991 as apprentice, then law clerk to Senior Justice Bellosillo where CJ met him in 1995, then court administrator from January 2010 -- will serve until his 70th birthday on February 16, 2036.
